ai.description: This 60–100 cm viper has a stout body with brown, tan, and black blotches. It features a distinct triangular head, vertical pupils, and a dark post-ocular stripe.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Ovophis monticola* is the presence of a single pair of large, shield-like internasals that contact each other on the snout.
ai.habitat: The Chinese Mountain Pit Viper inhabits moist, dense evergreen and broadleaf forests in the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chinese Mountain Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal and employs a "sit-and-wait" hunting strategy, remaining motionless for hours to ambush passing small mammals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ovophis monticola* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–15 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring and summer months in its Indian range.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ovophis monticola* occurs in Northeast India (e.g., Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim) across the Eastern Himalayas at elevations typically ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
